title: Redwood + VentraCloud joint solution tech sync

transcript:
Date: 2026-01-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55 min | Recorded: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Nguyen (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (VentraCloud CTO), Sam Lopez (VentraCloud Lead Eng), Jordan Miles (VentraCloud Product), Ellen Park (VentraCloud Security)

Summary: quick intro, then deep dive into how we list the joint solution in VentraCloud marketplace, the reference architecture for private/VPC setup, and the steps to run an initial benchmark for throughput/latency.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh, quick intros, i'm Alex Carter AE on the Redwood partnerships team, with Maya and Liam from SE. Priya do you want to kick off?
[00:18] Priya (VentraCloud): yeah thanks Alex. we are excited — we've had internal asks for a managed Redwood offering in our marketplace. primary ask is a private/VPC option and clear network diagrams for customers. also curious about how the billing/marketplace cut will work.
[00:36] Maya (Redwood SE): great, so today we'll cover marketplace checklist, reference arch for VPC deployment, and a high-level integration plan. We'll also talk perf/benchmarks and what we need from VentraCloud to run tests.
[00:50] Sam (VentraCloud): one thing to call out — for some enterprise customers we need dedicated capacity or the ability to pin models; is that something Redwood Dedicated supports?
[01:05] Alex (Redwood): yes, Redwood Dedicated is the reserved capacity offering; you can pin model versions and allocate GPU pools. we should capture that in the listing as an option: hosted api vs dedicated vs private.
[01:20] Jordan (VentraCloud): on the UX side customers want a 1-click marketplace deploy that sets up networking, service account, and credentials; how automated can that be?
[01:32] Liam (Redwood SE): we can provide a deployable reference template — terraform module or CloudFormation — that creates the infra on VentraCloud side and wires up service accounts, KMS roles, and routes to the Redwood control plane. for private/on-prem we ship a package and config that points to a customer-managed control plane.
[01:52] Priya: okay that sounds promising. on security, Ellen wants to confirm KMS/HSM, audit logs, and retention settings.
[02:01] Ellen (VentraCloud): yes on audit logs — customers need audit-forwarding to their SIEM and we need RBAC mapping to SSO. also encryption-at-rest with customer KMS keys.
[02:12] Maya: that's in our private deployment checklist — we support BYOK (bring your own key) and have audit log endpoints. we'll capture specifics in the reference arch doc.
[02:24] Alex: quick note — sometimes doc transcriptions will show K-V cash instead of KV cache, so forgive the typos later.
[02:32] Sam: ha, yeah i've seen that, nice.
[02:36] [Speaker 1]: um, marketplace listing — what metadata do you need from us?
[02:42] Alex: good Q — we need product description, supported deployment modes, pricing tiers, example SLA, and the reference arch diagram. also screenshots and a short video for the marketplace tile.
[02:57] Jordan: for pricing we want a recommended model: per-seat vs per-token vs committed capacity. any best practice?
[03:05] Maya: typically for marketplace we recommend clear tiers: self-serve hosted (usage-based per-token), dedicated (monthly commit), and an enterprise private SKU (license + support). we'll share a pricing template with examples.
[03:22] Priya: on the integration side, network-wise what ports and endpoints need to be opened?
[03:28] Liam: primarily HTTPS to the Redwood endpoints, and we do an initial handshake for model control plane. if we're doing private long-lived connections we use mTLS and a persistent peering. we'll add exact port lists to the doc.
[03:45] Sam: benchmark question — what perf numbers should we expect for a 2xA100 pool vs a single A100?
[03:52] Maya: that's workload dependent; we'll run a standard benchmark with the prompts you provide. but ballpark: with batching and proper KV caching you should see ~2.5-3x throughput improvements on multi-GPU vs single instance for long chat workloads. again we'll quantify this in the benchmark run.
[04:12] Priya: good. we also have customers asking about model provenance and evals — can Redwood provide verification or eval artifacts?
[04:20] Alex: yes we include model metadata and can provide eval reports and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. put that as a marketplace feature.
[04:29] Jordan: legal/contract question — marketplace MSA vs direct contract, how do you usually handle?
[04:35] Alex: often we start with the marketplace's commercial terms for listing, then for enterprise customers we route to an addendum/enterprise SOW. we'll connect legal teams to align.
[04:45] Ellen: for security checklist — do you have SOC2 artefacts and pen test reports?
[04:50] Maya: yes SOC2 type II, and a red team summary. we'll attach redacted reports and a security FAQ.
[04:58] Sam: what's the rough timeline to get a listing live once we have the docs?
[05:03] Alex: typical is 2-4 weeks: draft listing, security review, marketplace QA, and a test deploy. for reference arch and integration tests add another 1-2 weeks depending on engineering availability.
[05:16] Priya: good to know. on the reference arch, can we walk through the components?
[05:22] Maya: sure — at a high level: VentraCloud marketplace deploy creates a VPC, service account, KMS key binding (BYOK), and a peering/secure route to the Redwood serving endpoint or to a private cluster if using Redwood Private. we show optional components: dedicated GPU pool, autoscaling policy, and caching layer for prefix/KV cache. sample diagram will show subnets and flow.
[05:48] Sam: do you have automation for KV cache warm-up?
[05:52] Liam: we have prefetched cache techniques and continuous batching strategies. for chat-heavy workloads we recommend adaptive KV cache and an initial warmup prompt set. we'll include that in the perf run.
[06:05] Jordan: marketplace tile content — who will author the copy? do you want VentraCloud product to edit or should Redwood draft?
[06:12] Alex: Redwood can draft an initial listing and VentraCloud can iterate. we'll send a markdown draft and a short 60s demo video.
[06:20] Priya: great. next, rollout options — can a customer choose hosted initially and later migrate to dedicated or private?
[06:28] Maya: yes we support cross-environment rollouts. we also support model version pinning during migration and automatic fallback policies. we'll document migration steps.
[06:38] Sam: any gotchas around SSO? customers use SAML/Okta.
[06:42] Liam: we support SSO via SAML and OIDC, and RBAC mapping to provider groups. we'll need VentraCloud to provide IdP metadata for the integration tests.
[06:54] [Speaker 2]: legal and pricing follow-up — will you share the pricing template now?
[06:59] Alex: we'll attach a pricing spreadsheet in the follow-up email.
[07:03] Priya: on benchmarks — we want to test a medium chat workload, 8-12 turn dialogues, with context ~3k tokens. can you support that scenario?
[07:11] Maya: yes that's exactly the kind of benchmark we'll run with your prompt set. please share sample prompts and expected qps.
[07:20] Sam: regarding monitoring — does Redwood surface token-level cost and latency per call?
[07:25] Maya: yes Redwood Console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, traces and error analysis. we'll include a screenshot in the marketplace listing.
[07:37] Alex: quick pause — any red flags from VentraCloud side?
[07:41] Priya: only that we need clear MSA and that security artifacts come fast. otherwise this looks doable.
[07:48] Ellen: also need to validate data residency for EU customers — can the private deployment be hosted in our EU region?
[07:56] Liam: yes we support regional deployments; the reference arch will include region mapping and routing.
[08:03] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps then.
[08:06] Alex: recap: Redwood to send draft listing, pricing template, reference arch diagram. VentraCloud to send network/VPC diagram, SSO metadata, and security interrogatory. schedule deep-dive for perf tests.
[08:20] Priya: sounds good — let's aim for the docs by 1/20 and deep-dive week of 1/22.
[08:27] Alex: excellent. we'll follow up in email with the assets and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[08:33] [00:30:00] (note: middle of meeting contained a detailed whiteboard walkthrough of the reference architecture; transcript here shortened - see attached diagram link)
[30:05] Maya: (walkthrough) on the whiteboard, subnet A holds the control plane peering, subnet B holds the private inference workers, KMS integration sits in subnet C, and audit-forwarding goes to VentraCloud SIEM.
[31:00] Sam: can you share that whiteboard aspng?
[31:05] Maya: yes will share svg/pdf in follow-up.
[32:10] Priya: small question about billing — marketplace takes a percentage, can we show gross vs net pricing?
[32:18] Alex: we'll put an example in the pricing template and mark fields for gross/net.
[33:00] Jordan: i'd like a sample billing flow diagram for portal and invoice generation.
[33:10] Liam: we'll include a billing flow diagram in the reference pack.
[34:20] Ellen: one more on compliance — do you support customer-managed logging endpoints?
[34:26] Maya: yes log forwarding and retention policies are configurable; we'll note limits.
[36:00] Alex: ok final wrap — thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-ups.
[36:05] Priya: thanks all.

Attachments/Links: "Draft marketplace checklist (will be sent)", "Reference arch diagram (will be attached)"; short demo link: https://redwood.example.com/demo-clip (placeholder)

Action items (captured above). Next meeting: engineering deep-dive (integration tests) proposed week of 2026-01-22.

End of transcript.
